questions.question: What is the function of a catalyst in a chemical reaction?
options: It speeds up the reaction and is completely used up.
It slows down the reaction and is chemically changed.
It speeds up the reaction without being used up or chemically changed.
It prevents the reaction from happening at all.

questions.question: Which statement about catalysts is correct regarding their specificity?
options: The same catalyst can speed up any chemical reaction.
Catalysts are specific to particular reactions; different reactions require different catalysts.
Catalysts only work on reactions that involve water.
Catalysts only work if they are heated to extremely high temperatures.

questions.question: What are biological catalysts that speed up chemical reactions inside living cells called?
options: Enzymes
Hormones
Polymers
Reactants

questions.question: What happens when a more reactive metal is added to a solution containing a salt of a less reactive metal?
options: No reaction occurs because the less reactive metal is protected.
The more reactive metal will displace the less reactive metal from its salt.
The solution will turn into an acid.
Both metals will dissolve and form a gas.

questions.question: When magnesium is added to copper sulfate solution, what are the products of this displacement reaction?
options: Magnesium sulfate solution and copper
Magnesium oxide and copper sulfate
Copper oxide and magnesium sulfate
Copper hydroxide and hydrogen gas

questions.question: How can scientists use displacement reactions to confirm the order of metals in the reactivity series?
options: By measuring which metal produces the most smoke when burned.
By seeing which metals can displace other metals from their salt solutions.
By weighing the metals before and after they are heated in air.
By testing if the metals can conduct electricity.

questions.question: What is a metal ore?
options: A pure metal that has been polished.
A liquid metal found deep underground.
A type of rock that contains a metal in a form that can be extracted.
A synthetic alloy made in a factory.

questions.question: In which situation can carbon be used to extract a metal from its metal ore?
options: Only when the metal is more reactive than carbon.
When carbon is more reactive than the metal being extracted.
Carbon can extract any metal, regardless of reactivity.
Only when the ore is a liquid at room temperature.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the typical properties of metals?
options: They are good thermal and electrical conductors, strong, shiny, malleable, and ductile.
They are poor conductors of heat, brittle, dull, and soft.
They have low melting points, are transparent, and highly flexible.
They are always liquids that can be easily poured at room temperature.

questions.question: How do ceramics change when they are heated during their manufacturing process?
options: They remain soft and easily moldable.
They melt into a liquid and cannot solidify.
They turn from soft substances into hard and brittle materials.
They become highly flexible and ductile like metals.

questions.question: Which statement is true about plastics?
options: There is only one type of plastic and all plastics have identical properties.
They are made from polymers and there are many types of plastics with very different properties.
All plastics are natural materials harvested from trees.
Plastics cannot be molded into different shapes because they are too hard.

questions.question: What is an alloy?
options: A pure metal element that has been polished to a high shine.
A mixture of elements that includes at least one metal.
A compound made only of non-metal gases.
A type of plastic used to coat electrical wires.

questions.question: What is the purpose of combining materials to make a composite?
options: To make the material more difficult to recycle.
To create a new material with improved properties.
To ensure the material decays faster in the environment.
To turn a solid material into a gas.

questions.question: How are polymer molecules structured?
options: They consist of individual, unconnected single atoms.
They are made from small molecules called monomers joined to form very long chains.
They are giant three-dimensional metallic lattices.
They are simple diatomic molecules like oxygen.

questions.question: Why do some polymers have high melting points?
options: Because their molecules are hard to separate from each other.
Because they contain heavy metal atoms.
Because they are highly reactive with oxygen in the air.
Because they are made entirely of water molecules.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about the origin of polymers?
options: All polymers must be made synthetically in factories.
Polymers only exist in outer space.
Polymers can be made synthetically, but some also exist naturally.
Natural polymers do not exist; they are all artificial.

questions.question: What effect does adding a plasticiser have on a polymer?
options: It makes the polymer extremely brittle and easy to break.
It gets between polymer molecules and allows them to move over each other more easily.
It causes the polymer to immediately dissolve in water.
It joins all the polymer chains into a single rigid block.

questions.question: What is the effect of having cross-links between polymer molecules?
options: They make the polymer much softer and liquid-like.
They make the polymer harder and less flexible.
They lower the melting point to below room temperature.
They cause the polymer to conduct electricity like a metal.

questions.question: When a metal reacts with an acid, what are the products?
options: A metal salt and hydrogen gas.
A metal oxide and carbon dioxide.
A metal hydroxide and oxygen gas.
A metal carbonate and water.

questions.question: What are the products when certain metals react with water?
options: A metal oxide and nitrogen gas.
A metal hydroxide and hydrogen gas.
A metal salt and carbon dioxide.
Pure oxygen gas and an acid.
